summary: One read-only Codex cold read (gpt-5.6-terra, task-mu2cktur-l2bkmf) of the confirmed docs/specs/all-plants-statement.md against the built repo. Nine findings: one policy contradiction with accepted decision 0023, four underspecified contracts (master-version pin, drill pins for no-budget and partial-YTD plants, the cell state table, plant classification determinism), one false claim (statement audit-before-read), one hidden lifecycle assumption (partial actuals uploads), one stale-docs handover hazard, and one stale ledger line. Seven were settled from the repository and its decisions; the actuals-upload policy and the acceptance of decisions 0030-0032 went to the human in one round. The spec was amended once, in place, and this pass is bound to the amended digest.
gaps: Budget-upload policy contradicted accepted decision 0023: the spec refused a plant budget whose leaves did not match the format outline, while 0023 requires drift to load and be reported.
The mapping-master version was only named in the drill audit, not pinned: a deployment between rendering and drilling could resolve different triples and show a non-footing footer (deferral D-0038).

No-budget and partial-YTD drill provenance was underspecified: 'the plant budget batch where one exists' was singular, while a YTD block can involve several budget batches or none, and the shipped drill requires one budget batch to locate its outline.
The spec asserted statement reads are audit-before-read; MisStatementService executes governed blocks with no audit dependency (deferral D-0036), and no criterion made the claim testable.
Plant classification was not deterministic: 'name-normalised' matching against the format's Plant list was undefined while DHS/DHS2 versus DMHS was explicitly unresolved.
Later actuals uploads carried a hidden destructive assumption: replace-per-period with no stated outcome for a partial extract or an unknown plant.

The cell state table was incomplete: the shipped budget-present Roll-over state was not placed against the new absent-budget dash, and Ask's 'absent' Budget did not say null measure, omitted column or labelled cell.
The surrounding confirmed specs and architecture docs still describe the DUB-only, budget-owned-outline model, so a planner could inherit contradictory requirements.
contradictions: Spec versus decision 0023 on outline mismatch: refuse versus load-and-report.
Spec 'what does not change' claimed audit-before-read for all reads while the statement and export routes are un-audited (D-0036).
The brief's answer ledger said LLM/residency 'decide later' while accepted decision 0027 settled Bedrock in ap-south-1 — stale context, corrected, not re-asked.
resolutions: Repository-resolved by decision 0023: a plant budget whose leaves differ from the active format outline loads, the unattached leaves are named in its validation result, and only matching leaves attach. Decision 0030 was amended to say so before acceptance; the spec's Behaviour and criterion 6 now match.

Repository-resolved: the statement's provenance carries the mapping-master version, the drill sends it back, and a mismatch is refused as 'statement out of date'. Written into Behaviour and criterion 7; closes D-0038 in this story.

Repository-resolved: the drill pin contract is exactly one format outline batch covering the block end plus zero or more plant budget batches, one per loaded month. Written into Behaviour and criterion 7; decision 0030 names the same contract.
Repository-resolved: the audit-before-read claim is removed for the statement and export routes; the drill and Ask keep it; D-0036 stands and is named as not closed here.

Repository-resolved: classification is keyed on the SAP plant code alone through the committed classification table (decision 0031); the nursery flag is derived from the extract's cost centres with a table override; the format's Plant list is never used for matching; the fourteen July nursery codes are listed and proven by a hermetic test (new criterion 11).

HUMAN ROUND: actuals uploads stay replace-per-period and always activate; the validation result names plants missing versus the previously active batch and any unknown codes; the previous batch stays retained. Written into Behaviour and criterion 10.

Repository-resolved: the full cell state table is written — budget-present blocks keep the shipped Budget/% states and Roll-over's shipped 'unavailable' state; budget-absent blocks show the dash with the 'not loaded' label in all three; Ask renders an absent Budget as a null measure in a present column with the same label.

Repository-resolved: a 'Supersedes' section names the exact clauses of mis-selection-and-master, sap-financial-ingestion, financial-mis-statement, actuals-drill-down and the two architecture docs that decisions 0029/0030 override, citing decision precedence; D-0032's BRIEF reconciliation stays deferred as not in conflict.
HUMAN ROUND: decisions 0030, 0031 and 0032 accepted, confirmed by Rahul Anand, recorded with forge decision accept before this pass.
Ledger: decision 0027 governs residency unchanged; the stale 'decide later' line is not re-opened.
open_items: Non-blocking: whether DHS, DHS2 and Belagum in the format's Plant list are DMHS and two plants not yet in the extract — display names only.
Non-blocking: D-0036 (statement and export audit) stays deferred; D-0032 (BRIEF reconciliation) stays deferred.

rounds.question: Actuals uploads replace the whole month. With 31 plants that is safe only if every SAP export is company-wide. What should happen when a later upload for a month is missing plants that the current active batch has, or contains a plant the master does not know?

Three new decision records support this plan: 0030 (the format outline is its own ingest object; plant-keyed budget batches; drift reported per 0023, never blocked), 0031 (the master is generated by a committed script from the client's mapping sheet plus a plant classification table), 0032 (Ask clarifications resume a selection through a typed continuation, starting with plantChoice). Accept all three, confirmed by Rahul Anand?
